transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Product), Lisa Chen (Acme Head of Platform), Omar Khan (Acme Security), Priya Singh (Acme DevOps)

Summary:
Quick demo focused on data handling and retention controls in Redwood: logging redaction, PII detection, request storage toggles, and per-customer retention policies. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated/private options for regulated payments workloads. Agreed next steps: share security docs, pricing, and schedule POC benchmark.

Topics:
- Redwood API / Console / Optimize controls for request logging
- Automatic and configurable redaction options (PII regex, ML-based detection)
- Storage toggles: disable request body storage, store tokens-only, ephemeral request mode
- KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs
- Retention TTLs and legal hold/manual export

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Nina our SE and Marco from product. Quick intro?
[00:06] Lisa Chen: Hi all Lisa here. We're in payments infra, curious about how Redwood handles sensitive request data, PII, and retention controls.
[00:12] Omar Khan: Hi Omar, security on the platform team. Main question is can we prevent full request payloads from being stored and still run debugging?
[00:19] Nina Patel: Great question. We'll walk through Console toggles, API flags, and Optimize suggestions. There's tradeoffs — full logs help debugging and model qa, but you can apply redaction and turn off long-term storage.
[00:30] Marco Ruiz: And we'll show how Dedicated/private deployments change the defaults and give you control over where logs live and who holds keys.
[00:38] [00:40] Jordan Lee: Ok demo screen share — opening Redwood Console -> Settings -> Data & Retention. Note: some names may be slightly different in your tenant.
[00:46] [00:52] Nina Patel: First control: Request Storage Toggle. By default hosted tenants store request metadata, token counts, and short-lived request body for 30 days for debugging. You can flip this to "Disable Request Body storage" which redacts or omits bodies after processing.
[01:05] Priya Singh: When you say redact, is that full-body redact or field-level? We send cardholder and PII fields in JSON.
[01:12] Nina Patel: Both. There are three layers: 1) Automatic PII detection (ML-based patterns trained on common PII like emails, phone, SSNs), 2) Configurable regex-based redaction rules you can scope per-route, 3) Field-level allowlist where you can choose only to persist certain metadata fields. So you could automatically redact anything matching a payment card pattern and persist only metadata such as request_id and latency.
[01:30] Omar Khan: How reliable is the ML detection? We're worried about false negatives.
[01:35] Nina Patel: We surface confidence scores in the audit logs. If confidence below threshold, it flags for review. You can set strict mode where anything flagged even low-confidence is redacted. We also support customer-supplied redaction rules so you can add your own patterns.
[01:48] [02:00] Jordan Lee: Another option: store only anonymized embeddings or hashes derived from requests for analytics. That way you can do similarity search or quality monitoring without raw text.
[02:10] Lisa Chen: Embeddings-only sounds useful. Does that affect cost?
[02:13] Marco Ruiz: Slight additional compute to create embeddings but reduces storage and compliance risk. Redwood Optimize can recommend this for high-PII traffic.
[02:22] [03:00] Nina Patel: Now demo of redaction rules UI. You can add a regex rule per route or apply org-wide. Example we type: "(?i)card_number" and show preview where strings are masked with ****. The Console shows a live sample and also a test button to run sample payloads through the rules.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Nice. Is there an API to programmatically update rules? We prefer infra-as-code.
[03:25] Nina Patel: Yes, there is APIs and Terraform provider support for rules, retention TTLs, and audit log exports.
[03:32] [04:15] Omar Khan: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for compliance and export to our SIEM. What's available?
[04:20] Marco Ruiz: We have an Audit Logs export to S3 or to your syslog/SIEM via push. In Dedicated and Private deployments you control the S3 bucket and the KMS keys. Logs can be configured to include redaction metadata (what was redacted, confidence scores) without including the redacted content.
[04:38] Lisa Chen: Can we run legal hold so data beyond TTL is preserved for an investigation?
[04:42] Nina Patel: Yes — legal hold is a toggle at org level. When enabled it preserves a flagged set of requests and exports them to a locked bucket. Access is restricted and audit-tracked.
[04:52] [05:30] Jordan Lee: Let's show API flags. For the Redwood API you can set header x-redwood-store-request: false to prevent request body persistence for that call. Likewise, x-redwood-redact-level: strict | relaxed | none.
[05:45] Priya Singh: So the app can opt-out per request? That's great for payments flows.
[05:50] Nina Patel: Exactly. Also there's an account-level default and per-route overrides in the Console.
[06:00] [06:40] Omar Khan: KMS/HSM — we require customer-managed keys. How is data encrypted at rest and who rotates keys?
[06:46] Marco Ruiz: Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS keys or bring-your-own via AWS KMS/GCP Cloud KMS. For Dedicated/private you can use HSM with customer controls and full key rotation. Encryption in transit uses TLS and at rest uses AES-256 with keys tied to your KMS.
[07:05] Lisa Chen: What about logs that are exported to S3? Are they encrypted with our key?
[07:09] Marco Ruiz: Yes you can specify the bucket and the KMS key for export. Exports inherit your bucket policy and keys.
[07:16] [08:00] Jordan Lee: Quick note on performance: redaction and PII detection add a small CPU overhead but we optimize it — if you run high throughput payments we recommend offloading detection to an async process or use route-level allowlist to minimize per-request work. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and caching settings.
[08:20] Lisa Chen: So there's a tradeoff latency vs safety. We can't add a 100ms per request overhead on our critical path.
[08:27] Nina Patel: Understood — options: a) synchronous strict redaction (slower), b) immediate response with async redaction in background (faster but temporarily available in short-lived logs), c) never store bodies and only keep metadata.
[08:40] Priya Singh: For our use case we prefer async redaction + no long-term storage. We still need to be able to replay a small sample for debugging.
[08:49] Jordan Lee: You can configure a short retention window (e.g., 24 hours) and a "debug window" where logged raw payloads are accessible for a short time before redaction. After debug window expires, they're purged or redacted according to policy.
[09:00] [09:30] Marco Ruiz: Demo: show retention slider -> default 30 days, move to 1 day -> console warns about reduced debugging. Also show "Debug Access" role-based access control (RBAC) — only allowed roles can see unredacted payloads and every access is audited.
[09:45] Omar Khan: RBAC is important — can we sync with our SSO and map roles?
[09:50] Nina Patel: Yes SAML/SSO provisioning supported, SCIM for user sync, and you can map groups to RBAC roles.
[10:00] [10:40] Lisa Chen: For PCI concerns, do you have a PCI-specific config or guidance?
[10:44] Marco Ruiz: We have a PCI guidance doc and a recommended architecture for Dedicated/private infra where you disable body storage, use field-level masking, and route sensitive flows to private endpoints. We'll share the doc.
[10:55] Jordan Lee: Link: https://redwood.example.com/security/pci-guidance (shared in chat).
[11:05] [12:00] Priya Singh: About model evals and Optimize — if we disable storing bodies, can we still run quality monitoring?
[12:05] Marco Ruiz: Yes, two modes: 1) store ephemeral unlabeled samples for a short time and feed them into offline evals, 2) store hashed/anonymized versions or human-redacted variants for evals. Optimize can run A/B comparisons even with anonymized inputs.
[12:24] Omar Khan: Is there a way to automatically remove PII from training/eval datasets?
[12:28] Nina Patel: We have scrubbing pipelines that apply regex+ml filters and manual QA steps before datasets are used for any model improvement. Customers opt-in for sharing training data; default is no sharing.
[12:40] [13:15] Jordan Lee: Demo of audit log entry: shows event type, actor, redaction metadata (pattern id, confidence), and link to exported artifact. The event does not include raw content when redacted.
[13:30] Lisa Chen: Can audit logs be forwarded to Splunk?
[13:33] Marco Ruiz: Yep, syslog and S3 exports supported.
[13:40] [15:00] Priya Singh: One operational question: if we run a POC on Dedicated, how do we run benchmarks—are there scripts?
[15:08] Nina Patel: We have benchmark harnesses and a recommended dataset template. For POC we usually run 24-72 hour throughput and latency tests and run the request storage toggles to validate retention behavior. We'll provide the harness.
[15:30] Jordan Lee: We'll also propose a minimal test that includes synthetic PII payloads to verify redaction.
[15:40] Omar Khan: Regulator may ask for proof of deletion. How do we demonstrate deletion?
[15:45] Marco Ruiz: We provide deletion receipts: a signed manifest showing request IDs deleted, timestamp, and KMS key id. For Dedicated/private we can provide more detailed chain-of-custody logs.
[16:00] [17:10] Lisa Chen: Any competitors that do this well? We looked at OpenAI and Anthropic but their default storage policies differ.
[17:18] Jordan Lee: Right — many providers store raw inputs by default for improvements, though they offer opt-outs. Redwood emphasizes explicit toggles, org policies, and Dedicated/private options for stricter control.
[17:30] Priya Singh: Cost question: does Dedicated increase cost for these controls?
[17:35] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated incurs reserved capacity costs but gives you stronger controls and no commingled storage. For high-PII workloads it's often cheaper long-term due to lower audit/compliance overhead. We'll include pricing scenarios.
[17:50] [20:00] Jordan Lee: Quick Q&A — Omar any remaining security concerns?
[20:05] Omar Khan: Mainly want to review the SOC2 and architecture diagrams, and see the KMS integration doc.
[20:10] Nina Patel: We'll share SOC2 report and an architecture diagram for Dedicated.
[20:15] Lisa Chen: Also want an exported sample showing how redaction metadata looks for our SIEM ingestion.
[20:20] Jordan Lee: We'll send a sanitized sample export.
[20:30] [22:00] Recap and next steps:
- Share SOC2 & security pack (Nina)
- Send Dedicated pricing and proposed POC scope (Jordan)
- Provide benchmark harness and sample redaction dataset (Marco + Priya)
- Schedule POC kickoff (TBD: week of 2025-02-24)

Links shared in chat:
- https://redwood.example.com/security/pci-guidance
- https://redwood.example.com/soc2-report (placeholder)
